034133c4-42d2-45af-9db6-351eadfd5a1e.content:
We've given dialogue starting elements a custom element attribute:

tag: dialogue_start

This way, the game engine knows where to look for each NPC's dialogue start.

We've used this solution in the Unreal Engine demo game.

Right click the element and choose "Properties," to see it.

3701967c-5c90-4474-8838-39d634d1ebf7.content:
Just as with dialogue starts, we've given dialogue ending elements a custom element attribute:

tag: dialogue_end

This way, the game engine knows not to follow the [Back] connections, which are for Arcweave's Play Mode playability only.

Right click these elements and choose "Properties," to see the tag attribute.

43cf8efd-f69f-421b-b65e-227b0b29a37f.content:
These are the elements that the game engine must look for:

1. They are in the Starting Board (which has custom id: starting_dialogue_elements—see board's properties).
2. They have the relevant NPC's character component attached.

We are using this solution in the Godot & Unity demo games.
